hero.title: Siksha ‘O’ Anusandhan
hero.summary: Siksha ‘O’ Anusandhan’s Institute of Agricultural Sciences offers undergraduate and specialist postgraduate study in Bhubaneswar. Crop sciences, resources and extension sit within a broad departmental structure. Documented village attachment work in Khordha district and a rice-research collaboration give students concrete links with farming communities and agricultural research.

overview.heading: Agriculture learning through departments, villages and research
paragraphs: SOA’s Institute of Agricultural Sciences lists departments spanning agricultural engineering, economics, extension, crop production, plant protection and horticulture. The 2026 programme list describes a four-year agriculture bachelor’s degree and two-year master’s routes, providing both a broad foundation and routes into specialised study.

A 2026 university report describes village attachment in Khordha district, where students assessed cropping systems and worked on village action plans. Another 2026 report records an ICAR-CRRI partnership concerning rice research and postgraduate training. These are documented examples of academic activity; access to a particular research placement still depends on the programme and arrangements in force.

admissions.heading: Applying to SOA
admissions.intro: SOA publishes a dedicated 2026 agriculture eligibility page. Bachelor’s and master’s applicants face different subject, marks/OGPA and minimum-age requirements. The SAAT 2026 merit framework explicitly includes B.Sc. and M.Sc. Agriculture, with rank-based counselling subject to seats.
eligibility_points: 2026 bachelor’s entry: English with PCM/PCB/PCMB; 60% General/OBC or 50% SC/ST/PH; minimum age 16 on 31 August 2026.
2026 master’s entry: B.Sc. Agriculture/Horticulture; 60% General/OBC or 50% SC/ST, with published OGPA alternatives; minimum age 19 on 31 August 2026. Eligibility marks cannot be rounded.

faqs.question: What is IAS at SOA?
faqs.answer: IAS is the Institute of Agricultural Sciences, SOA’s agriculture teaching and research unit.

faqs.question: How long are the 2026 agriculture degrees?
faqs.answer: The bachelor’s programme is four years; the listed agriculture master’s programmes are two years.

faqs.question: Does undergraduate study include rural exposure?
faqs.answer: A 2026 university report documents village attachment activity in Khordha district.

faqs.question: What does the ICAR-CRRI agreement concern?
faqs.answer: The 2026 report describes collaboration in rice research, training and postgraduate research support.

faqs.question: What is the ICAR term here?
faqs.answer: The audited Faculty of Agricultural Sciences record runs from 29 July 2024 to 28 July 2029.

faqs.question: Are the 2026 fee amounts verified?
faqs.answer: The official fee index is available, but its linked academic-fee document could not be read in this research session.
